doc.title: Requirements engineering
doc.body:
Q: What is requirements elicitation?
A: Gathering what stakeholders need through interviews, surveys and observation.

Q: Functional versus non-functional requirement?
A: Functional says what the system does. Non-functional says how well, like speed or security.

Q: What makes a requirement testable?
A: It is specific and measurable, so you can write a pass or fail check.

Q: Name one risk of vague requirements.
A: Scope creep, and a build nobody agrees is finished.

doc.title: Exam 2 review: chapters 5 to 8
doc.body:
Q: What does a use case diagram show?
A: Actors and the goals they achieve with the system.

Q: Include versus extend?
A: Include is always part of the base case. Extend is optional and conditional.

Q: What does a UML class diagram show?
A: Classes, their attributes and operations, and the relationships between them.

Q: When do you use a sequence diagram?
A: To show how objects exchange messages over time in one scenario.

Q: Which flow did our group take?
A: The checkout flow.

title: Design patterns flashcards
summary: Five cards on Observer, Factory and Strategy from Thursday's lecture.

doc.title: Design patterns
doc.body:
Q: What is the Observer pattern?
A: One subject notifies many observers when its state changes.

Q: Where do you see Observer in real code?
A: Event listeners and subscriptions.

Q: What does the Factory pattern hide?
A: Which concrete class gets created.

Q: Who calls a factory method?
A: The caller, asking for a type and getting an object back.

Q: Which pattern is on the exam only?
A: Strategy.
